\chapter{About Yourself}
\label{ch:te-about-yourself}
\hlchaptermodality{89}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask and answer about a job, the languages someone speaks, whether they are married, and an address.}

Complete TE-C89-address: the questions that come after a name.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[udyōgaṁ]{\te{ఉద్యోగం} (udyōgaṁ) — a job}

\label{lesson:TE-C89-job}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a person, then the Telugu for a relative.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఉద్యోగం}}
\textbf{\te{ఉద్యోగం}} (\emph{udyōgaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a job\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మీ} \te{ఉద్యోగం} \te{ఏమిటి}?} — \textquotedblleft{}what is your job?\textquotedblright{}. It is built exactly like \textbf{\te{మీ} \te{పేరు} \te{ఏమిటి}?}, with the job where the name was.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The second question of an introduction, on the frame of the first.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udyōgaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udyōgaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{mī udyōgaṁ ēmiṭi?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a person, then the Telugu for a relative, then say \emph{udyōgaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఉద్యోగం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A job\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bhāṣa]{\te{భాష} (bhāṣa) — a language}

\label{lesson:TE-C89-language}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a relative, then the Telugu for a job.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{భాష}}
\textbf{\te{భాష}} (\emph{bhāṣa}) — \textquotedblleft{}a language\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మీకు} \te{ఏ} \te{భాషలు} \te{వచ్చు}?} — \textquotedblleft{}which languages do you know?\textquotedblright{}. The knower sits in the dative, as in \textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{తెలుగు} \te{వచ్చు}}: a language is something that comes to you.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to ask what someone speaks, in the frame you learned for Telugu itself.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhāṣa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhāṣa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{mīku ē bhāṣalu vaccu?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a relative, then the Telugu for a job, then say \emph{bhāṣa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{భాష} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A language\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[iṅglīṣu]{\te{ఇంగ్లీషు} (iṅglīṣu) — English}

\label{lesson:TE-C89-english}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a job, then the Telugu for a language.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఇంగ్లీషు}}
\textbf{\te{ఇంగ్లీషు}} (\emph{iṅglīṣu}) — \textquotedblleft{}English\textquotedblright{}, the language.

\textbf{\te{నాకు} \te{ఇంగ్లీషు} \te{వచ్చు}, \te{తెలుగు} \te{కొంచెం} \te{వచ్చు}} — \textquotedblleft{}I know English, and a little Telugu\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An honest answer to which languages do you know.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṅglīṣu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṅglīṣu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nāku iṅglīṣu vaccu, telugu koñcem vaccu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a job, then the Telugu for a language, then say \emph{iṅglīṣu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఇంగ్లీషు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}English\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[peḷḷi]{\te{పెళ్ళి} (peḷḷi) — a wedding, marriage}

\label{lesson:TE-C89-wedding}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a language, then the Telugu for English.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{పెళ్ళి}}
\textbf{\te{పెళ్ళి}} (\emph{peḷḷi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a wedding\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}marriage\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మీకు} \te{పెళ్ళి} \te{అయిందా}?} — \textquotedblleft{}are you married?\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}has a wedding happened to you?\textquotedblright{}. The person sits in the dative again, and the marriage is something that happened.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A question you will be asked early and often, and the word it turns on.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peḷḷi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peḷḷi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{mīku peḷḷi ayindā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a language, then the Telugu for English, then say \emph{peḷḷi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{పెళ్ళి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wedding, marriage\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cirunāmā]{\te{చిరునామా} (cirunāmā) — an address}

\label{lesson:TE-C89-address}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for English, then the Telugu for a wedding.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{చిరునామా}}
\textbf{\te{చిరునామా}} (\emph{cirunāmā}) — \textquotedblleft{}an address\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మీ} \te{చిరునామా} \te{ఏమిటి}?} — \textquotedblleft{}what is your address?\textquotedblright{}. The same frame as the name and the job: \textbf{\te{మీ} ... \te{ఏమిటి}?}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Job, languages, marriage, address: the questions that come after a name.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cirunāmā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cirunāmā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{mī cirunāmā ēmiṭi?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for English, then the Telugu for a wedding, then say \emph{cirunāmā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{చిరునామా} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An address\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
